intro: Covers the US session of Thursday 29 October. This brief was delayed from 07:15 to re-check sources. The SPI 200 futures sources differ on the size of the move, so it is shown as a range, and the European session and ECB/Bank of Japan outcomes could not be verified.
footnotes: US index closes and 10-year yield from Yahoo Finance (S&P 500 and Nasdaq moves match Trading Economics commentary); VIX from Yahoo Finance (single source).
Gold is the Trading Economics CFD spot price (-1.00%); Yahoo's gold futures showed US$4,039.60 (-0.30%).
Brent is the Trading Economics price; a Yahoo summary put the close near US$115.
The 10-year yield change is Yahoo's; it implies a 5.0% level a day earlier.
AUD/USD and iron ore are Trading Economics CFD reference prices.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures (December contract) are indicated higher by roughly 0.3-0.6%, at about 8,925-8,932 (TradingView 8,925, +0.30%/+0.39%; Investing.com 8,932, +0.57%). Taking the midpoint of about +0.44%, that implies an ASX 200 open near 8,931, around +39 points (+0.44%), with a range of roughly +27 to +51 points. Note the futures gain sits alongside a weaker Nasdaq; the futures change likely includes the ASX day session, in which the index closed up. The ASX 200 closed Thursday at 8,891.8, up 44.5 points (+0.50%).

local_events: ABS producer price index for Q3 (previous +1.3% q/q, +3.6% y/y), about 11:30 AEDT (time inferred)
Private sector credit for September (previous +0.6% m/m, consensus +0.5%), about 11:30 AEDT (time inferred)
No RBA events are scheduled today
what_moved: A 12.6% fall in Alphabet after its results, which showed negative free cash flow as capital spending climbed, dragged the Nasdaq down 1.4% and revived concerns about AI spending. The broader S&P 500 lost only 0.3%: health care hit a record high on Eli Lilly's raised forecast and small caps rallied (the Russell 2000 rose about 1% by midday), while Caterpillar fell on its sales outlook. Strong US growth (Q3 GDP +3.4% annualised) and sticky inflation (September PCE +3.6% y/y) kept rate-hike expectations alive. Sector-by-sector percentages were not available.

news.headline: Alphabet's slide pulls the Nasdaq lower.
news.summary: Alphabet fell 12.64% to US$283.82, wiping about US$500bn from its value, after reporting negative free cash flow of US$9.1bn despite strong cloud growth.

news.headline: Fed holds, two dissent for a hike.
news.summary: The Federal Reserve left rates unchanged on Wednesday, with two members dissenting in favour of a hike amid sticky inflation. The target range and full vote count were not verified.

news.headline: US growth accelerates, inflation stays high.
news.summary: The advance estimate put Q3 US GDP growth at 3.4% annualised, up from 2.2% in Q2, while the September PCE price index rose 3.6% from a year earlier.

news.headline: Caterpillar drops on outlook; Lilly lifts health care.
news.summary: Caterpillar beat estimates but fell on its sales outlook, while Eli Lilly raised its full-year revenue forecast after revenue grew 39% to US$24.4bn, taking the S&P 500 health care sector to a record.

news.headline: Oil stays elevated on US-Iran diplomacy.
news.summary: Brent traded around US$115-116/bbl as traders weighed efforts to avert a restart of US strikes on Iran; details come from a summary of the live blog and were not independently verified.

news.headline: Australian inflation hotter ahead of the RBA.
news.summary: September CPI rose 4.3% y/y (previous 4.0%) and trimmed mean 3.6%, ahead of the RBA's decision on Tuesday; Trading Economics lists the previous cash rate at 4.60% with a 4.85% forecast.

coming_up: Tonight (Friday, 8:30am ET) the US Q3 employment cost index is due. The RBA interest rate decision is on Tuesday 3 November at about 2:30pm AEDT, the same day as the US midterm elections. The US payrolls release date was not verified.
